Are triangles \(\triangle {@t1a@}{@t1b@}{@t1c@}\) and \(\triangle {@t2a@}{@t2b@}{@t2c@}\) congruent?

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

[[ if test="isP" ]][[ if test="iscong" ]]

Yes — the triangles are congruent.

In parallelogram \({@va@}{@vb@}{@vc@}{@vd@}\), opposite sides are equal, so \({@va@}{@vd@} = {@vc@}{@vb@}\), and opposite angles are equal, so \(\angle {@va@} = \angle {@vc@}\).

Because \({@vd@}{@ve@} \parallel {@vb@}{@vf@}\), the points \({@ve@}\) and \({@vf@}\) sit symmetrically, which forces \({@va@}{@ve@} = {@vc@}{@vf@}\).

Two sides and the included angle now match, so \(\triangle {@t1a@}{@t1b@}{@t1c@} \cong \triangle {@t2a@}{@t2b@}{@t2c@}\) by SAS. (Equivalently, a half-turn about the centre of the parallelogram carries one triangle exactly onto the other.)

[[ else ]]

No — the triangles are not congruent.

We still have \({@va@}{@vd@} = {@vc@}{@vb@}\) (opposite sides) and \(\angle {@va@} = \angle {@vc@}\) (opposite angles). But \({@ve@}\) and \({@vf@}\) are not placed symmetrically — the segments \({@vd@}{@ve@}\) and \({@vb@}{@vf@}\) are not parallel — so \({@va@}{@ve@} \neq {@vc@}{@vf@}\).

Two matching parts are equal but the third differs, so the triangles are not congruent.

[[/ if]][[/ if]][[ if test="isK" ]][[ if test="iscong" ]]

Yes — the triangles are congruent.

The diagonal \({@va@}{@vc@}\) is the axis of symmetry of the kite. We are given \({@va@}{@vb@} = {@va@}{@vd@}\) and \({@vc@}{@vb@} = {@vc@}{@vd@}\), and \({@va@}{@vc@}\) is common to both triangles.

Therefore \(\triangle {@t1a@}{@t1b@}{@t1c@} \cong \triangle {@t2a@}{@t2b@}{@t2c@}\) by SSS.

[[ else ]]

No — the triangles are not congruent.

Both triangles stand on the shared base \({@vd@}{@vb@}\). Vertex \({@va@}\) is equidistant from \({@vd@}\) and \({@vb@}\), and so is \({@vc@}\), so each triangle is isosceles on that base.

However \({@va@}{@vd@} \neq {@vc@}{@vd@}\) (the kite is not a rhombus), so the equal sides have different lengths in the two triangles. They are not congruent — even though they look alike.

[[/ if]][[/ if]][[ if test="isTr" ]][[ if test="iscong" ]]

Yes — the triangles are congruent.

The trapezium is isosceles, so the legs are equal, \({@va@}{@vd@} = {@vb@}{@vc@}\), and therefore the diagonals are equal, \({@va@}{@vc@} = {@vb@}{@vd@}\).

Triangles \(\triangle {@t1a@}{@t1b@}{@t1c@}\) and \(\triangle {@t2a@}{@t2b@}{@t2c@}\) share the base \({@vd@}{@vc@}\), have equal legs, and equal diagonals, so they are congruent by SSS.

[[ else ]]

No — the triangles are not congruent.

This trapezium is not isosceles: the legs \({@va@}{@vd@}\) and \({@vb@}{@vc@}\) have different lengths, so the diagonals \({@va@}{@vc@}\) and \({@vb@}{@vd@}\) are unequal too.

The two triangles share the base \({@vd@}{@vc@}\) but their other sides differ, so they are not congruent.

[[/ if]][[/ if]]
